title: Guard spec v1 — bug replay
description: Would this suite have caught the bugs that actually escaped? For each fix commit in a range: revert only the source to its parent, remove the test the fix shipped, run what remains. `blind` means the suite was blind to a bug that really shipped. Unlike an injected fault, a replayed bug is ground truth — a human already confirmed it was a defect — which is what makes this the oracle a fault model is calibrated against.

range.description: The commit range searched for fix commits, as given.

candidates.description: Fix commits found in the range before de-duplication by patch-id.

duplicates.description: Commits dropped as the same patch under another sha. A dual-branch topology carries the same fix two or three times; counting it twice corrupts the corpus.

patchId.description: `git patch-id --stable` of the fix: the identity of the CHANGE rather than of the commit. A dual-branch topology carries the same fix under several shas, and counting it twice corrupts the corpus. Hex, 40 characters for a SHA-1 repository and 64 for a SHA-256 one; the commit sha when git could not compute one.

subject.description: The fix commit's subject line, for a human reading the corpus.

verdict.description: `caught` = a remaining test failed by assertion on the reverted source, every run. `blind` = the suite stayed green on known-broken code. `nocover` = no test exercises the reverted files at all, which is worse than blind. `unverifiable` = nothing could be concluded: the revert did not apply, the suite could not load, it timed out, or the commit only ADDS source (`no-prior-version` — there is no earlier behaviour to have been blind to, so it is not a bug the suite could have caught and it never enters a calibration). `flaky` = the runs disagreed, so nothing can be concluded.

source.description: Source files reverted to the fix's parent.

removedTests.description: Test files the fix shipped, removed before the run: the fix's own test proves nothing about what the suite knew before it.

faultClass.description: The injected-fault class this real diff most resembles, derived mechanically from the diff shape. This is the join key between ground truth and a fault model: it is what lets P(this fault class is a real bug) be computed.
